name: Buick 3800 Series II L36 (naturally aspirated, 1995-2005)
summary: 90-degree pushrod V6 made even-firing by split crank pins offset 30 degrees, so it fires every 120 degrees despite the V8-derived bank angle; fitted with a balance shaft.

bank_angle_deg.note: 'Engine Type 90* V6' from a 1998 Camaro service manual as transcribed on 3800wiki.

rod_length_mm.note: Not found. Wikipedia says only that Series II rods were shortened 1 in versus Series I. 3800wiki notes L36/L26 rods are longer than supercharged L67/L32 rods.

firing_order.note: Numbering (Wikipedia): cylinders 1-3-5 on the left-hand bank (front bank in transverse FWD cars), 2-4-6 on the right-hand bank, number 1 furthest from the flywheel. Firing therefore alternates banks every time.

crank.value: split-pin: each of the three throws carries two crank pins offset 30 degrees from each other
crank.note: Wikipedia describes the 30-degree split-pin crank as introduced in 1977 and says the Series II crankshaft was 'redesigned' without giving a new offset; 30 degrees is what a 90-degree V6 needs for even firing. Balance shaft added from the 1988 LN3 onward.

firing_intervals_deg.note: Even fire, per Wikipedia's description of the split-pin crank ('even-firing'). The 120 figure for a 30-degree split on a 90-degree V6 is also stated on Wikipedia's V6 engine page.

intake_valve_dia_mm.note: Parts-catalogue valve table. Agrees with Wikipedia's 1.8 in for Series II.

exhaust_valve_dia_mm.note: Parts-catalogue valve table covering 1996-2009 applications. Wikipedia says 1.52 in (38.6 mm) exhaust valves were introduced on 2003 engines, so 36.6 mm applies to earlier L36; the catalogue does not make that split.

cam_lobe_lift_intake_mm.note: LOBE lift, not valve lift, from the 1998 Camaro service manual as transcribed. Rocker ratio was not found on an opened page, so valve lift is left null.

intake_lift_mm.note: Valve lift not found; needs rocker ratio times 6.55 mm lobe lift.

exhaust_lift_mm.note: Valve lift not found; needs rocker ratio times 6.48 mm lobe lift.

intake_duration_deg.note: At 0.050 in lifter rise. Enthusiast wiki cam comparison table, row 'Stock L36/L26'; no primary source cited there. LSA listed as N/A for the L36 (115 for the supercharged L67).

peak_power_kw.note: 205 hp; converted by me. rpm not stated on the page. wbodytech.com says W-body calibrations were 200-205 hp.

peak_power_rpm.note: Not found on an opened page.

peak_torque_rpm.note: Not found on an opened page.

missing: cam timing events and lobe separation

sources.what: 3800wiki general mechanical specifications, stated as copied from a 1998 Camaro (L36) service manual. Bore, stroke, CR, firing order, lobe lift.
3800wiki camshaft comparison table (enthusiast-maintained). Stock duration at .050.
Wikipedia, Buick V6 engine. Split-pin crank, numbering, Series II changes, power.
EJC Performance parts guidebook page for the GM 3.8 Series II. Valve head diameters.
W-body enthusiast wiki; power range and intake description.
Wikipedia, V6 engine: 30-degree split pins give even 120-degree intervals on a 90-degree V6.

vehicle.name: Buick LeSabre Custom (2000)

curb_kg.note: 'Curb weight 3,567 lbs.' for the '2000 Buick LeSabre Custom - Sedan 3.8L V6 auto'; converted by me. A period review of a 2000 LeSabre Limited gives 'Curb Weight 3627 pounds' (https://www.theautochannel.com/vehicles/new/reviews/2000/solo0006.html).

gear_count.note: 'A smooth-shifting and seemingly bulletproof four-speed automatic transmission is the sole gearbox available'. The spec database calls it a '4-speed electronically-controlled automatic transmission w/OD'; that it is the 4T65-E is from Wikipedia's 4T65-E article and the spec database's matching ratios (inference).

gears.note: Wikipedia 4T60-E/4T65-E article, 'Gear ratios: 1 2.921, 2 1.568, 3 1.000, 4 0.705, R 2.385'. The carspecs.us page for this car lists 'First Gear Ratio 2.92, Second 1.57, Third 1.00, Fourth 0.75, Reverse 2.39'; the fourth-gear figure disagrees (0.75 vs 0.705). The 1998 Regal GS page on the same database gives 0.71, so 0.75 looks like a database error (my judgement).

final_drive.note: 'Final Drive Axle Ratio 2.86'. Wikipedia lists 4T65 'Diff Ratio 2.86, 3.05, 3.29'. The 2000 review says LeSabres with the 'optional Gran Touring package get a higher axle ratio'.

wheel_radius_m.note: Calculated by me from the tyre size (half the rim diameter plus section width times aspect ratio): the unloaded geometric radius, not a published rolling radius; the loaded rolling radius is a few percent smaller.

tyre.note: 'Front Tire Size P215/70R15 ... Rear Tire Size P215/70R15'. Front-wheel drive, so the front tyre is the driven one.

top_speed_kmh.note: Omitted. The only figure found, 'Top-speed 105 mph', is from a review of a LeSabre Limited on 'P225/60R16 touring tires', not the Custom modelled here.

driven.note: English Wikipedia, 'Buick LeSabre' (read 2026-11-17), infobox layout: FR layout (1959-1985), Front-engine, front-wheel drive (1986-2005).

missing: a GM document for the 2000 LeSabre's axle ratio and curb weight (only a spec database found)

sources.what: carspecs.us page '2000 Buick LeSabre Custom - Sedan 3.8L V6 auto': gear ratios, final drive, tyres, curb weight. Spec database, no source given.
Wikipedia article on the GM 4T60-E/4T65-E transaxle: gear ratios and available differential ratios.
The Auto Channel review 'Buick LeSabre Limited (2000)' by Tom Hagin, with a specification box: sole gearbox, Limited curb weight and top speed.
